AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Transform: AWS::Serverless-2016-10-31
Description: Worker Appointment Scheduling – single-table, multi-tenant backend

##############################################################################
# Parameters – IDs of your already-existing Cognito pool + client
##############################################################################



Parameters:
  ExistingUserPoolId:
    Type: String
    Description: us-east-2_GDqu3Yx7v

  ExistingUserPoolClientId:
    Type: String
    Description: 5gcfno4cq49o9vddo8b85308qd

  EvoBaseUrl:                      # ← NEW
    Type: String
    Description: Base URL of your Evolution-API cluster
    Default: https://evolution-api-production-ad04.up.railway.app   # or leave blank & pass in

  EvoApiKey:                       # ← NEW
    Type: String
    NoEcho: true                   # hides value in CloudTrail/console
    Description: API key for Evolution-API


##########################################################################
# Resources
##########################################################################

Resources:

##############################################################################
# 1)  Authenticated HTTP API (Cognito)  – existing admin / dashboard API
##############################################################################

  WorkerHttpApi:
    Type: AWS::Serverless::HttpApi
    Properties:
      StageName: Prod
      CorsConfiguration:
        AllowOrigins:
          - "http://localhost:3000"
          - "https://calendario.aisol.cloud"
          - "https://d24qdqpj5ro3r2.cloudfront.net"
        AllowMethods: ["OPTIONS", "GET", "POST", "PUT"]
        AllowHeaders: ["*"]
      Auth:
        Authorizers:
          CognitoAuthorizer:
            IdentitySource: "$request.header.Authorization"
            JwtConfiguration:
              Issuer:   !Sub "https://cognito-idp.${AWS::Region}.amazonaws.com/${ExistingUserPoolId}"
              Audience: [!Ref ExistingUserPoolClientId]

##############################################################################
# 2)  Public REST API  (share-link + WhatsApp) – API-Key protected
##############################################################################

  AppPublicApi:
    Type: AWS::Serverless::Api
    Properties:
      StageName: Prod
      EndpointConfiguration: REGIONAL
      Cors: "'*'"

  AppPublicApiKey:
    Type: AWS::ApiGateway::ApiKey
    DependsOn: AppPublicApiProdStage
    Properties:
      Enabled: true
      Name: public-booking-key
      StageKeys:                      # ← link key directly to the stage
        - RestApiId: !Ref AppPublicApi
          StageName: Prod

  PublicApiFunction:
    Type: AWS::Serverless::Function
    Properties:
      CodeUri: .
      Handler: app.public_handler
      Runtime: python3.11
      MemorySize: 256
      Timeout: 15
      Environment:
        Variables:
          APPOINTMENTS_TABLE: !Ref AppointmentsTable
          WORKERS_TABLE:      !Ref WorkersTable
          CONFIGS_TABLE:      !Ref ConfigsTable
      Policies:
        - DynamoDBCrudPolicy: { TableName: !Ref AppointmentsTable }
        - DynamoDBCrudPolicy: { TableName: !Ref WorkersTable }
        - DynamoDBCrudPolicy: { TableName: !Ref ConfigsTable }
      Events:
        PublicConfig:
          Type: Api
          Properties:
            RestApiId: !Ref AppPublicApi
            Path:   /public/config
            Method: GET
        PublicWorkers:
          Type: Api
          Properties:
            RestApiId: !Ref AppPublicApi
            Path:   /public/workers
            Method: GET
        PublicBook:
          Type: Api
          Properties:
            RestApiId: !Ref AppPublicApi
            Path:   /public/appointments/book
            Method: POST

##############################################################################
# 3)  DynamoDB tables
##############################################################################

  AppointmentsTable:
    Type: AWS::DynamoDB::Table
    Properties:
      TableName: !Sub "${AWS::StackName}-Appointments"
      BillingMode: PAY_PER_REQUEST
      AttributeDefinitions:
        - AttributeName: shop_id
          AttributeType: S
        - AttributeName: sort_key
          AttributeType: S
      KeySchema:
        - AttributeName: shop_id
          KeyType: HASH
        - AttributeName: sort_key
          KeyType: RANGE

  WorkersTable:
    Type: AWS::DynamoDB::Table
    Properties:
      TableName: !Sub "${AWS::StackName}-Workers"
      BillingMode: PAY_PER_REQUEST
      AttributeDefinitions:
        - AttributeName: shop_id
          AttributeType: S
        - AttributeName: worker_id
          AttributeType: S
      KeySchema:
        - AttributeName: shop_id
          KeyType: HASH
        - AttributeName: worker_id
          KeyType: RANGE

  ConfigsTable:
    Type: AWS::DynamoDB::Table
    Properties:
      TableName: !Sub "${AWS::StackName}-Configs"
      BillingMode: PAY_PER_REQUEST
      AttributeDefinitions:
        - AttributeName: shop_id
          AttributeType: S
      KeySchema:
        - AttributeName: shop_id
          KeyType: HASH

##############################################################################
# 4)  Authenticated Lambda (existing)
##############################################################################

  WorkerApiFunction:
    Type: AWS::Serverless::Function
    Properties:
      CodeUri: .
      Handler: app.lambda_handler
      Runtime: python3.11
      Environment:
        Variables:
          APPOINTMENTS_TABLE: !Ref AppointmentsTable
          WORKERS_TABLE:      !Ref WorkersTable
          CONFIGS_TABLE:      !Ref ConfigsTable
      Policies:
        - DynamoDBCrudPolicy: { TableName: !Ref AppointmentsTable }
        - DynamoDBCrudPolicy: { TableName: !Ref WorkersTable }
        - DynamoDBCrudPolicy: { TableName: !Ref ConfigsTable }
      Events:
        ApiGet:
          Type: HttpApi
          Properties:
            ApiId:  !Ref WorkerHttpApi
            Path:   /{proxy+}
            Method: GET
            Auth:
              Authorizer: CognitoAuthorizer
        ApiPost:
          Type: HttpApi
          Properties:
            ApiId:  !Ref WorkerHttpApi
            Path:   /{proxy+}
            Method: POST
            Auth:
              Authorizer: CognitoAuthorizer
        ApiPut:
          Type: HttpApi
          Properties:
            ApiId:  !Ref WorkerHttpApi
            Path:   /{proxy+}
            Method: PUT
            Auth:
              Authorizer: CognitoAuthorizer

  # 5) Whatsapp inntegration:

  # tiny HTTP API — no auth, CORS '*'
  WhatsAppInApi:
    Type: AWS::Serverless::HttpApi
    Properties:
      StageName: Prod
      CorsConfiguration:
        AllowOrigins: ["*"]
        AllowMethods: ["POST"]
        AllowHeaders: ["*"]

  WhatsAppInFunction:
    Type: AWS::Serverless::Function
    Properties:
      CodeUri: whatsapp_in_py
      Handler: whatsapp_in.lambda_handler
      Runtime: python3.11
      MemorySize: 256
      Timeout: 15
      Environment:
        Variables:
          EVO_BASE_URL: !Ref EvoBaseUrl
          EVO_API_KEY:  !Ref EvoApiKey
          PUBLIC_API_URL: !Sub "https://${AppPublicApi}.execute-api.${AWS::Region}.amazonaws.com/Prod"
          PUBLIC_API_KEY: rE4H9alXxFaDjcRRp8vGv9ran0H5z4RW8SGNTtDP
      Events:
        EvoWebhook:
          Type: HttpApi          # ← DIFFERENCE
          Properties:
            ApiId: !Ref WhatsAppInApi
            Path: /whatsapp-in
            Method: POST


  WhatsAppConnect:                # POST /whatsapp/connect
    Type: AWS::Serverless::Function
    Properties:
      Runtime: python3.11
      Handler: whatsapp_admin.connect_handler
      CodeUri: . 
      Timeout: 20
      Environment:
        Variables:
          EVO_BASE_URL:   !Ref EvoBaseUrl    # make these Parameters
          EVO_API_KEY:    !Ref EvoApiKey
          CONFIGS_TABLE:  !Ref ConfigsTable
      Policies:
        - DynamoDBCrudPolicy:
            TableName: !Ref ConfigsTable
        - Statement:       # allow outbound https
            - Effect: Allow
              Action: "execute-api:Invoke"
              Resource: "*"
      Events:
        Api:
          Type: HttpApi
          Properties:
            ApiId: !Ref WorkerHttpApi
            Path:   /whatsapp/connect
            Method: POST
            Auth:
              Authorizer: CognitoAuthorizer   # owner only
  WhatsAppLists:                  # PATCH /whatsapp/lists
    Type: AWS::Serverless::Function
    Properties:
      Runtime: python3.11
      Handler: whatsapp_admin.lists_handler
      CodeUri: . 
      Timeout: 10
      Environment:
        Variables:
          CONFIGS_TABLE: !Ref ConfigsTable
      Policies:
        - DynamoDBCrudPolicy: { TableName: !Ref ConfigsTable }
      Events:
        Api:
          Type: HttpApi
          Properties:
            ApiId: !Ref WorkerHttpApi
            Path:   /whatsapp/lists
            Method: PATCH
            Auth:
              Authorizer: CognitoAuthorizer


##############################################################################
# 5)  Outputs
##############################################################################

Outputs:

  AdminApiUrl:
    Description: Cognito-protected HTTP API
    Value: !Sub "https://${WorkerHttpApi}.execute-api.${AWS::Region}.amazonaws.com/Prod"

  PublicApiUrl:
    Description: Public REST API (API-Key required)
    Value: !Sub "https://${AppPublicApi}.execute-api.${AWS::Region}.amazonaws.com/Prod"

  PublicApiKey:
    Description: API key for /public/* endpoints
    Value: !Ref AppPublicApiKey

1. **Main Directories**:
   - `/shop-frontend`: React frontend application
   - `/shop-backend`: Express/AWS Lambda backend

   - Finite State Machine (FSM) for booking flow

# Refactoring Summary

## Overview

This project underwent a comprehensive refactoring to improve code organization, maintainability, and performance. The refactoring focused on two main areas:

1. **LoginPage Component**: Split into smaller components and hooks
2. **ConfigContext**: Restructured into a modular organization
3. **Chatbox Component**: Complete restructuring of the 2850-line component into smaller, reusable components and custom hooks

## Key Improvements

### 1. LoginPage Refactoring

- **Component Extraction**:
  - Created `LoginHeader`, `CalendarPreview`, `FeatureBadges`, and `LoginFooter` components
  - Created `LoginContainer` to manage the UI composition

- **Custom Hooks**:
  - Implemented `useAuth` hook to handle authentication logic
  - Implemented `useCalendar` hook to handle calendar data generation

- **Benefits**:
  - Improved component reusability
  - Clear separation of concerns
  - Enhanced maintainability with smaller, focused components
  - Memoization for performance optimization

### 2. ConfigContext Refactoring

- **Module Organization**:
  - Extracted default configurations to a dedicated file
  - Created a custom hook for state management (`useConfigState`)
  - Implemented a clean interface with entry point file

- **Benefits**:
  - Better code organization
  - Improved maintainability
  - Separation of configuration data from state logic
  - Cleaner imports with index file

### 3. Chatbox Component Refactoring

- **Component Hierarchy**:
  - Created `ChatHeader`, `MessageList`, `MessageItem`, `ChatInput`, and `QuickReplyOptions` components
  - Implemented a new main component `NewChatbox` with clean composition

- **Custom Hooks**:
  - `useChatState`: Manages messages and chat interactions
  - `useBookingState`: Handles booking flow state
  - `useGuidedMode`: Manages guided vs free mode interactions

- **Utilities**:
  - `dateUtils.js`: Date and time formatting functions
  - `chatUtils.js`: Message formatting helpers
  - `bookingUtils.js`: Appointment creation utilities

- **Benefits**:
  - Dramatically reduced component size (2850 lines → modular structure)
  - Clear separation of concerns
  - Improved testability with smaller, focused components
  - Enhanced maintainability
  - Better performance through optimized rendering

## Implementation Approach

1. **Analysis Phase**:
   - Identified problematic components
   - Analyzed state management and data flow
   - Created a comprehensive refactoring plan

2. **Incremental Implementation**:
   - Refactored LoginPage first as a proof of concept
   - Restructured ConfigContext to improve state management
   - Created the foundation for Chatbox refactoring with utilities and hooks
   - Implemented UI components with proper PropTypes

3. **Best Practices Applied**:
   - Component composition for UI structure
   - Custom hooks for logic separation
   - Prop validation with PropTypes
   - Memoization for performance optimization
   - Clear naming conventions

   ```javascript

input.content:
# Responsive Design Improvements

## Overview

The codebase has been enhanced to provide a consistent and optimized user experience across both web and mobile devices. This was achieved through comprehensive refactoring, focusing on responsive design principles and flexible layouts.

## Key Improvements

### 1. Centralized Style Management

- **Shared Style Files**: Created central style files (`chatStyles.js` and `loginStyles.js`) to maintain consistency
- **Responsive Breakpoints**: Implemented consistent responsive breakpoints across components
- **Theme Integration**: Utilized MUI theme system for better consistency and maintainability

### 2. Mobile Optimizations

- **Text Sizing**: Adjusted font sizes based on screen size - smaller on mobile, normal on desktop
- **Element Spacing**: Reduced padding and margins on mobile for more compact layout
- **Component Sizing**: Scaled down UI elements for better fit on smaller screens
- **Touch Targets**: Ensured interactive elements are appropriately sized for touch interfaces

### 3. Layout Improvements

- **Flexible Containers**: Used responsive box models that adapt to different screen sizes
- **Stack Adaptations**: Modified stacks and flexbox layouts to handle resizing properly
- **Simplified UI**: Streamlined interface on smaller screens while maintaining functionality

### 4. Component-Specific Enhancements

#### Chat Interface:

- **Message Bubbles**: Optimized spacing and sizing of message bubbles
- **Input Area**: Made input field and buttons adapt to screen size
- **Quick Replies**: Enhanced quick reply options for better touch interaction
- **Header**: Streamlined header component for mobile viewing

#### Login Page:

- **Calendar Preview**: Adjusted size of calendar elements for mobile screens
- **Feature Badges**: Optimized display of feature chips on smaller screens
- **Login Button**: Enhanced button size and text for better mobile usability
- **Error Messages**: Improved error display across all screen sizes

### 5. Accessibility Improvements

- **Color Contrast**: Used theme colors to ensure proper color contrast
- **Touch Targets**: Sized buttons and interactive elements appropriately for touch
- **ARIA Attributes**: Added aria-label to improve screen reader compatibility
- **Responsive Typography**: Implemented a responsive type system that scales with screen size

### 6. Performance Considerations

- **Reduced Repaints**: Centralized styles to minimize DOM changes
- **Simplified DOM**: Reduced nested elements where possible
- **Optimized Rendering**: Used React.memo and proper component structure

## Testing Approach

The responsive design has been designed to work especially well on:

1. **Mobile Phones**: Optimized for screens 320px-480px wide
2. **Tablets**: Works well on mid-size screens 768px-1024px
3. **Desktop**: Full experience on screens 1024px and larger

## Implementation Details

The implementation follows the MUI responsive design system using breakpoints:
- `xs`: 0-600px (Mobile phones)
- `sm`: 600-960px (Tablets/small laptops)
- `md`: 960-1280px (Laptops)
- `lg`: 1280px+ (Desktops)

All responsive styles use the object notation pattern with breakpoints:

```javascript
// Example responsive style
{
  fontSize: { xs: '0.85rem', sm: '0.95rem', md: '1rem' },
  padding: { xs: 1, sm: 2 },
  width: { xs: '100%', sm: 'auto' }
}
```

## Future Improvements

1. **Advanced Animations**: Add responsive animations that work well on both mobile and desktop
2. **Device-Specific Features**: Implement touch-specific features for mobile users
3. **Progressive Enhancement**: Add advanced features for desktop while maintaining a sleek mobile experience

- `xs`: 0-600px (Mobile phones)
- `sm`: 600-960px (Tablets/small laptops)
- `md`: 960-1280px (Laptops)
- `lg`: 1280px+ (Desktops)

All responsive styles use the object notation pattern with breakpoints:

# WhatsApp Integration Guide - Text-Based Numbered Options

## Overview

This guide explains how the chatbot interacts with WhatsApp using text-based numbered options since the Evolution API does not support clickable buttons.

## How Text-Based Numbered Options Work

Instead of presenting clickable buttons to users, the chatbot now formats options as numbered lists in text messages. Users can respond with the number corresponding to their choice.

### Example Interaction:

```
Bot: Qual serviço você gostaria de agendar?

1. Corte de cabelo
2. Barba
3. Corte e barba
4. Sobrancelha
5. Hidratação

User: 1

Bot: Qual profissional você prefere para o serviço de Corte de cabelo?

1. João Silva
2. Maria Oliveira
3. Pedro Costa

User: 2

Bot: Para qual data você gostaria de agendar com Maria Oliveira?

(Date options shown)

[...]

Bot: Para confirmar: Corte de cabelo com Maria Oliveira em 2025-05-20 às 14:30. Está correto? (Responda sim para confirmar)

1. Sim
2. Não

User: 1

Bot: ✅ Agendamento confirmado! Obrigado por escolher nossos serviços.
```

## Technical Implementation

The implementation involves three key components:

1. **Formatting Responses with Numbered Options**:
   - When options are available (services, workers, confirmation), the chatbot formats the message with numbered options.
   - Each option is presented as a line with a number, followed by the option text.

2. **Processing Numeric Input**:
   - When a user sends a message containing only a number, the system interprets it as a selection.
   - The number is mapped to the corresponding option (array index + 1).
   - The selected option is then passed to the FSM for processing.

3. **Context Management**:
   - The system maintains a conversation context for each user.
   - This context includes the current step, selected options, and available choices.
   - The context is preserved between messages to maintain conversation state.

## Code Components

### Key Functions in JavaScript (index.mjs):

- `formatReplyWithNumberedOptions(reply, context)`: Adds numbered options to replies when applicable.
- `processUserInput(text, context)`: Converts numeric responses to corresponding option texts.
- `userContexts` Map: Stores conversation context for each user.

### Key Functions in Python (whatsapp.in.py):

- `format_reply_with_numbered_options(reply, ctx)`: Adds numbered options to replies.
- `process_user_input(text, ctx)`: Handles numeric responses.
- `USER_CONTEXTS` dictionary: Stores conversation states.

## Integration with Booking FSM

The numbered options system works with the existing Finite State Machine (FSM):

1. The FSM manages the conversation flow and booking logic.
2. The WhatsApp integration layer:
   - Adds numbered options to outgoing messages.
   - Converts incoming number responses to option text.
   - Passes the processed text to the FSM.

## Benefits of Text-Based Numbered Options

1. **Universal Compatibility**: Works on all WhatsApp clients without requiring special features.
2. **Simple User Experience**: Intuitive for users - just type a number to select.
3. **Lower Technical Requirements**: No need for button support in the messaging API.
4. **Consistent Behavior**: Provides a predictable interaction pattern through the entire conversation.

## Maintenance Considerations

- When adding new options to the FSM, ensure they are properly numbered in the formatting functions.
- If the FSM steps change, update the option processing logic to handle the new steps correctly.
- Consider adding validation and error handling for out-of-range numeric inputs.

# WhatsApp Interaction Example with Numbered Options

This document provides examples of typical interactions with the chatbot using text-based numbered options on WhatsApp.

## Example 1: Complete Booking Flow (Individual Account)

### Initial Greeting:
```
User: Olá

Bot: Olá! Sou Amanda, assistente virtual da Barbearia Elite. Qual é o seu nome, por favor?

User: Carlos

Bot: Olá Carlos! Qual serviço você gostaria de agendar?

1. Corte de cabelo
2. Barba
3. Corte e barba
4. Sobrancelha
5. Hidratação
```

### Service Selection (using number):
```
User: 1

Bot: Para qual data você gostaria de agendar seu Corte de cabelo com João Silva?
```

### Date Selection:
```
User: 2025-05-20

Bot: Qual horário você prefere no dia 2025-05-20?

1. 09:00
2. 09:30
3. 10:00
4. 10:30
5. 11:00
6. 11:30
```

### Time Selection:
```
User: 2

Bot: Para confirmar: Corte de cabelo com João Silva em 2025-05-20 às 09:30. Está correto? (Responda sim para confirmar)

1. Sim
2. Não
```

### Confirmation:
```
User: 1

Bot: ✅ Agendamento confirmado! Obrigado por escolher nossos serviços.
```

## Example 2: Complete Booking Flow (Enterprise Account)

### Initial Greeting:
```
User: Oi

Bot: Olá! Sou Amanda, assistente virtual da Barbearia Elite. Qual é o seu nome, por favor?

User: Maria

Bot: Olá Maria! Qual serviço você gostaria de agendar?

1. Corte de cabelo
2. Barba
3. Corte e barba
4. Sobrancelha
5. Hidratação
```

### Service Selection (using text instead of number - both work):
```
User: Barba

Bot: Qual profissional você prefere para o serviço de Barba?

1. João Silva
2. Pedro Costa
3. Ana Ferreira
```

### Worker Selection:
```
User: 2

Bot: Perfeito! Qual data você prefere para agendar com Pedro Costa?
```

### Date Selection:
```
User: 2025-05-21

Bot: Qual horário você prefere no dia 2025-05-21?

1. 14:00
2. 14:30
3. 15:00
4. 15:30
5. 16:00
```

### Time Selection:
```
User: 2

Bot: Para confirmar: Barba com Pedro Costa em 2025-05-21 às 14:30. Está correto? (Responda sim para confirmar)

1. Sim
2. Não
```

### Confirmation:
```
User: 1

Bot: ✅ Agendamento confirmado! Obrigado por escolher nossos serviços.
```

## Example 3: Error Handling

### Out-of-range selection:
```
User: 9

Bot: Desculpe, não entendi. Poderia escolher uma opção da lista?

1. Corte de cabelo
2. Barba
3. Corte e barba
4. Sobrancelha
5. Hidratação
```

### Date format validation:
```
User: amanhã

Bot: Formato de data inválido. Use AAAA-MM-DD, por favor.
```

### Time format validation:
```
User: 2 horas

Bot: Formato de horário inválido. Use HH:MM, por favor.
```

## Benefits for the User

1. **Simple interaction**: Just type a number to select an option
2. **Works on all devices**: No need for special WhatsApp features
3. **Consistent experience**: Same interaction pattern throughout the conversation
4. **Fallback to text**: Users can still type the full option text if they prefer
5. **Clear choices**: Numbered lists make options easy to understand and select

## Notes for Implementers

- The system accepts both number inputs and full text matches
- Error handling is built in to guide users who input invalid selections
- Context is maintained throughout the conversation
- Users can cancel and restart at any point by typing "cancelar"

            RestApiId: !Ref AppPublicApi

        - AttributeName: shop_id

##############################################################################

      Environment:
        Variables:
          EVO_BASE_URL: !Ref EvoBaseUrl
          EVO_API_KEY:  !Ref EvoApiKey
          PUBLIC_API_URL: !Sub "https://${AppPublicApi}.execute-api.${AWS::Region}.amazonaws.com/Prod"
          PUBLIC_API_KEY: rE4H9alXxFaDjcRRp8vGv9ran0H5z4RW8SGNTtDP
      Events:
        EvoWebhook:
          Type: HttpApi          # ← DIFFERENCE
          Properties:
            ApiId: !Ref WhatsAppInApi
            Path: /whatsapp-in
            Method: POST


  WhatsAppConnect:                # POST /whatsapp/connect
    Type: AWS::Serverless::Function
    Properties:
      Runtime: python3.11
      Handler: whatsapp_admin.connect_handler
      CodeUri: . 
      Timeout: 20
      Environment:
        Variables:
          EVO_BASE_URL:   !Ref EvoBaseUrl    # make these Parameters

# WhatsApp Integration with Text-Based Numbered Options

This implementation integrates the booking FSM with WhatsApp using Evolution API, providing a text-based numbered option interface since Evolution API doesn't support clickable buttons.

## How It Works

1. **Text-based Numbered Options**: Instead of buttons, the system presents options as a numbered list
2. **Number-to-Option Translation**: When a user sends a number (e.g., "1"), the system translates it to the corresponding option text
3. **FSM Compatibility**: This approach maintains compatibility with the existing FSM by translating before processing

## Example Flow

### Service Selection Step

```
Bot: Olá João! Qual serviço você gostaria de agendar?

1. Corte de cabelo
2. Barba
3. Corte e barba
4. Sobrancelha
5. Hidratação

User: 1

[System translates "1" to "Corte de cabelo" before passing to FSM]
```

### Worker Selection Step

```
Bot: Qual profissional você prefere para o serviço de Corte de cabelo?

1. Carlos
2. Marcelo
3. Roberto

User: 2

[System translates "2" to "Marcelo" before passing to FSM]
```

### Confirmation Step

```
Bot: Para confirmar: Corte de cabelo com Marcelo em 2025-05-15 às 14:30. Está correto? (Responda sim para confirmar)

1. Sim
2. Não

User: 1

[System translates "1" to "sim" before passing to FSM]
```

## Implementation Details

### Key Components

1. **NumberedOptions Utility** (`numbered-options.js` / `numbered_options.py`)
   - Formats FSM replies with numbered options based on the current step
   - Processes user input to convert numbers to corresponding text options
   - Manages user context between interactions

2. **Context Management**
   - Maintains conversation state for each user
   - Uses a key format: `{shopId}:{phoneNumber}`
   - Includes TTL to automatically expire old contexts

3. **Webhook Handler** (`index.js` / `whatsapp_in.py`)
   - Receives messages from Evolution API
   - Processes them through the FSM
   - Formats replies with numbered options
   - Sends responses back to WhatsApp

## Integration Flow

1. **Receive Message**:
   - Get message from Evolution API webhook
   - Extract user phone and message text

2. **Process Input**:
   - Retrieve user's context (or create new)
   - Convert numeric input to corresponding text options

3. **Run FSM**:
   - Pass processed text to FSM
   - Get reply and updated context

4. **Format Reply**:
   - Add numbered options to FSM reply
   - Add formatting hints for date/time steps

5. **Send Response**:
   - Send formatted reply to WhatsApp via Evolution API
   - Store updated context for next interaction

## Benefits

- **Maintains FSM Logic**: No changes needed to the core FSM implementation
- **User-Friendly**: Clear numbered options make it easy for users to respond
- **Flexible**: Works with any WhatsApp provider that doesn't support buttons

## Implementation Notes

- The implementation is available in both JavaScript (Node.js) and Python
- TTL (Time To Live) for contexts prevents memory leaks
- Each language implementation follows the same principles but with language-specific idioms
- Error handling and logging are implemented for better debugging

Based on my analysis of the codebase, here's a comprehensive breakdown of the WhatsApp integration requirements:

## WhatsApp Integration Requirements Analysis

### 1. Configuration and Environment Variables

**Required Environment Variables:**
- `EVO_BASE_URL`: Base URL of the Evolution API server (e.g., https://evolution-api-production-ad04.up.railway.app)
- `EVO_API_KEY`: API key for authenticating with Evolution API
- `PUBLIC_API_URL`: URL for the public API endpoints
- `PUBLIC_API_KEY`: API key for accessing public endpoints

**Frontend Configuration:**
- WhatsApp business phone number (format: +551199999999)
- Instance name for Evolution API (shown to use "teste" as default)
- Filter mode settings (whitelist/blacklist for numbers)

### 2. Evolution API Integration

**Integration Method:**
- The system uses the Evolution API as a middleware to connect with WhatsApp
- No direct WhatsApp Business API connection; Evolution API handles this

**Key API Endpoints:**
- `/instance/create`: Creates a WhatsApp instance
- `/instance/connect`: Generates QR code for connection
- `/instance/fetchInstances`: Lists available instances
- `/message/send`: Sends messages to WhatsApp users

**Connection Process:**
1. Generate QR code through Evolution API
2. User scans QR with WhatsApp mobile app
3. Connection established between Evolution API and WhatsApp
4. Webhook configured to receive incoming messages

### 3. WhatsApp Connection Setup Steps

1. **Configure Environment Variables**:
   - Set `EVO_BASE_URL` and `EVO_API_KEY` in deployment
   - Configure API Gateway for webhook endpoint

2. **Evolution API Instance Setup**:
   - Create instance via API with shop_id as instanceId
   - Configure webhook URL to point to Lambda function

3. **QR Code Generation and Scanning**:
   - Generate QR through Evolution API
   - Scan QR with WhatsApp mobile app within 45 seconds
   - Verify connection status

4. **Webhook Configuration**:
   - Ensure Evolution API sends messages to the correct webhook URL
   - Configure API Gateway to invoke Lambda function

### 4. Implementation Gaps and Potential Issues

1. **Hard-coded Values**:
   - Frontend component has hard-coded Evolution API URL and key
   - Instance name is hard-coded as "teste" which may cause conflicts

2. **Error Handling**:
   - Limited error handling for Evolution API connection failures
   - No automatic reconnection mechanism if WhatsApp disconnects

3. **Security Concerns**:
   - API key is exposed in frontend code
   - No validation or rate limiting on the webhook endpoint

4. **Scalability Considerations**:
   - In-memory context storage lacks persistence
   - No database backup for conversation state

5. **Webhook Configuration**:
   - The webhook URL in the QR code generation includes `${process.env.API_URL}/public/whatsapp-webhook`
   - This must be properly configured and accessible from Evolution API

6. **Multi-Tenant Confusion**:
   - Uses instanceId as shop_id which could cause issues in multi-tenant setup
   - Potential for cross-shop message mixing if not properly isolated

## Technical Implementation Details

1. **Numbered Options System**:
   - Custom implementation to work around Evolution API's lack of button support
   - Formats options as numbered lists
   - Translates numeric responses to option text before processing

2. **Finite State Machine (FSM)**:
   - Booking flow maintained in an FSM
   - State persisted between interactions
   - Steps: greeting → client name → service → worker → date → time → confirmation

3. **Context Management**:
   - Maintains conversation state
   - Uses in-memory storage with TTL (time to live)
   - Key format: `{shopId}:{phoneNumber}`

4. **Lambda Function Architecture**:
   - Receives webhook calls from Evolution API
   - Processes messages through FSM
   - Returns formatted responses

## Summary of Key Requirements

1. **External Services**:
   - Evolution API instance (self-hosted or cloud service)
   - WhatsApp Business account or personal account for testing

2. **Configuration**:
   - Evolution API credentials 
   - Webhook URL configuration
   - AWS environment variables

3. **Setup Process**:
   - Deploy backend with required environment variables
   - Configure Evolution API instance
   - Generate and scan QR code
   - Test end-to-end flow

4. **Maintenance**:
   - Monitor WhatsApp connection status
   - Update QR code if disconnected
   - Handle Evolution API updates/changes

The integration uses a numbered options approach to work around Evolution API's limitations, creating a text-based numbered menu system that allows users to interact via simple numeric responses while maintaining compatibility with the existing booking FSM.

### 1. Evolution API Integration Requirements

1. **Evolution API Instance**:
   - You need access to an Evolution API server
   - The frontend currently has a hardcoded URL: `https://evolution-api-production-ad04.up.railway.app`
   - A hardcoded API key: `429683C4C977415CAAFCCE10F7D57E11`

2. **Environment Variables**:
   - In production, these should be set in your backend deployment:
     - `EVO_BASE_URL`: Base URL of the Evolution API server
     - `EVO_API_KEY`: Your Evolution API authentication key
     - `PUBLIC_API_URL`: URL for your public API endpoints
     - `PUBLIC_API_KEY`: API key for accessing public endpoints

3. **WhatsApp Business Phone Number**:
   - You need a valid phone number to connect to WhatsApp
   - This must be entered in the WhatsApp configuration panel

### 2. Connection Setup Process

1. **QR Code Generation**:
   - Through the admin interface, go to WhatsApp configuration
   - Enable the WhatsApp integration
   - Enter your WhatsApp Business phone number
   - Click "Generate QR Code for Connection" 
   - The system will connect to Evolution API to generate a QR code

2. **WhatsApp Connection**:
   - Once the QR code appears, you have 45 seconds to scan it
   - Open WhatsApp on your phone
   - Go to Settings → Linked Devices → Link a Device
   - Scan the QR code to establish the connection

3. **Webhook Configuration**:
   - The system sets up a webhook automatically during instance creation
   - Make sure your Lambda/backend is properly deployed and accessible
   - The webhook URL should be: `${process.env.API_URL}/public/whatsapp-webhook`

### 3. Known Issues to Address

1. **Hardcoded Credentials**:
   - The frontend has hardcoded Evolution API credentials (lines 102-104 in WhatsAppConfig.js)
   - In production, you should move these to proper environment variables

2. **Instance Name**:
   - The instance name is hardcoded as "teste" (line 100 in WhatsAppConfig.js)
   - This should be unique per business to avoid conflicts

3. **Security Concerns**:
   - API keys are visible in frontend code - this should be handled by the backend only
   - No verification of incoming webhook calls

### 4. Advanced Configuration

1. **Message Filtering**:
   - You can configure whitelist or blacklist mode for phone numbers
   - Add specific phone numbers to filter lists
   - Enable/disable group message responses

2. **Integration with Ads**:
   - For click-to-WhatsApp ads, you can configure campaign IDs
   - This requires additional setup in Facebook Ads Manager

### Action Items to Make It Work

1. **Evolution API Setup**:
   - Ensure you have access to an Evolution API instance
   - Get your API credentials and set them properly
   - Consider setting up your own Evolution API server for better security

2. **Configuration Updates**:
   - Update the frontend code to remove hardcoded credentials
   - Ensure environment variables are properly set in backend deployment

3. **WhatsApp Phone**:
   - Ensure your WhatsApp Business number is valid and active
   - Keep the phone connected and online for consistent operation

4. **Testing Cycle**:
   - Set up the connection through QR code
   - Send test messages to verify the entire flow
   - Check both incoming and outgoing message processing

content.text:
Based on my analysis of the codebase, the whitelist/blacklist functionality for WhatsApp numbers is **not currently working**. 

The whitelist/blacklist configuration exists in the frontend UI and gets saved to the database, but there is no code in the backend that actually implements the filtering logic. When a WhatsApp message comes in, the handler doesn't check if the sender's phone number is in the whitelist or blacklist.

The key issues are:

1. The `index.js` file in the `/shop-backend/whatsapp_in/` directory processes all incoming WhatsApp messages without checking the filter settings.

2. After retrieving the shop configuration from the database, the code never checks the `config.messaging.whatsappIntegration.filterMode` or `filterNumbers` properties.

3. There's no conditional logic that would block messages from numbers that aren't in a whitelist or are in a blacklist.

To make the whitelist/blacklist functionality work properly, you would need to add code to the handler that:
- Retrieves the whitelist/blacklist configuration
- Checks incoming phone numbers against that configuration
- Decides whether to process or ignore messages based on the filter settings

I can provide a specific code implementation to add this functionality if you'd like to implement it now.

content.text:
Great! I've implemented the whitelist/blacklist functionality for WhatsApp number filtering. Here's what the implementation does:

1. **Early Number Filtering**:
   - Fetches shop configuration at the beginning of the handler
   - Checks if the WhatsApp sender should be allowed to proceed
   - Returns early with a success status if the number should be blocked

2. **Filtering Logic**:
   - Whitelist mode: Only allows numbers in the list
   - Blacklist mode: Blocks numbers in the list
   - Handles empty lists (empty whitelist blocks all, empty blacklist allows all)
   - Blocks group messages if the disableGroups setting is enabled

3. **Normalized Phone Number Comparison**:
   - Removes non-digit characters to ensure consistent matching
   - Handles partial matches for flexibility (e.g., comparing with/without country code)

4. **Optimizations**:
   - Avoids redundant config fetching
   - Reuses config data for context building
   - Returns minimal responses for blocked messages

This implementation should work with the existing frontend configuration, allowing you to:
1. Enable/disable WhatsApp integration
2. Choose whitelist or blacklist mode
3. Add phone numbers to filter
4. Enable/disable group message handling

To test it, configure your whitelist/blacklist in the admin UI and try sending WhatsApp messages from different numbers. The logs will show which messages are allowed or blocked based on your configuration.

## 1. Component Structure Optimization

### High Priority: Chatbox Component
- **Status**: Partially refactored (NewChatbox.js exists but old version still present)
- **Action**: Complete migration to new component structure
  - Delete the original 2,850 line Chatbox.js after verifying NewChatbox.js has all functionality

  - Old: `/src/context/ConfigContext.js`
  - New: Modular structure in `/src/context/config/`
- **Action**: Complete migration to modular version
  - Remove redundancy while maintaining backward compatibility
  - Update all imports to use the new structure

## 2. Code Duplication and Redundancy

### High Priority: WhatsApp Integration
- **Issue**: Duplicated filtering logic between frontend and backend
- **Action**: Create shared utility functions
  - Move `checkNumberFilter` to a shared module in `/shared/utils/`

- **Issue**: Repetitive error handling and mock mode handling
- **Action**: Extract common patterns
  - Create higher-order functions for API calls
  - Implement a centralized error handling strategy
  - Reduce boilerplate with a request wrapper function

### Low Priority: Style Definitions
- **Issue**: Duplicate styles across multiple components
- **Action**: Move to centralized theme
  - Extract common styles to theme provider
  - Use theme-based styling for consistency

## 3. Code Quality Improvements

### High Priority: Booking State Machine
- **Issue**: Overlapping responsibilities between chat components and FSM
- **Action**: Better separation of concerns
  - Clearly define FSM boundaries
  - Move business logic out of UI components
  - Simplify state transitions

### Medium Priority: Commented Code and Console Logs
- **Issue**: Numerous console.log statements and commented code in production
- **Action**: Clean up codebase
  - Remove all console.log statements except critical debugging
  - Remove commented code that's no longer needed
  - Add proper structured logging for important operations

### Low Priority: Type Safety
- **Issue**: Missing or incomplete PropTypes definitions
- **Action**: Enhance type safety
  - Add PropTypes to all components consistently
  - Consider transitioning to TypeScript for better static analysis

## 4. Architectural Optimization

### High Priority: Configuration Management
- **Issue**: Multiple overlapping configuration methods
- **Action**: Unify configuration strategy
  - Consolidate localStorage, sessionStorage, and API-based config
  - Implement a single source of truth for configuration
  - Create clear layers for different config types (default, shop, user)

### Medium Priority: Service Integration
- **Issue**: Coupling between service implementations
- **Action**: Create proper abstraction layers
  - Abstract API dependencies into interface-based services
  - Implement clear dependency injection

### Low Priority: State Management
- **Issue**: Mix of different state management approaches
- **Action**: Standardize state management
  - Use React Context and custom hooks consistently
  - Reduce prop drilling with proper context usage

## 5. Performance Optimizations

### High Priority: Render Optimization
- **Issue**: Excessive re-renders in chat components
- **Action**: Apply memoization
  - Use React.memo for functional components
  - Apply useMemo and useCallback hooks for expensive operations
  - Optimize state update patterns to minimize renders

### Medium Priority: Bundle Size
- **Issue**: Large dependency footprint
- **Action**: Reduce bundle size
  - Analyze bundle with tools like webpack-bundle-analyzer
  - Remove unused dependencies
  - Use dynamic imports for code splitting
  - Lazy load components where appropriate

## Implementation Strategy

1. **Step 1: Reduce Technical Debt First**
   - Complete the Chatbox refactoring
   - Remove duplicate code and commented-out sections
   - Finalize the ConfigContext migration

2. **Step 2: Shared Logic Extraction**
   - Create shared WhatsApp utilities

   - Move booking FSM logic to appropriate layers

3. **Step 3: Configuration Consolidation**
   - Unify configuration management 
   - Clarify configuration hierarchy
   - Improve default configurations

4. **Step 4: Optimize for Performance**
   - Apply React optimization techniques
   - Implement code splitting
   - Add component lazy loading

5. **Step 5: Modernize Architecture**
   - Consider TypeScript migration
   - Implement cleaner service abstractions
   - Apply consistent coding patterns

  - Implement clear dependency injection

  - Use React Context and custom hooks consistently
  - Reduce prop drilling with proper context usage

- **Action**: Apply memoization
  - Use React.memo for functional components
  - Apply useMemo and useCallback hooks for expensive operations
  - Optimize state update patterns to minimize renders

  - Remove unused dependencies

  const guidedMode = config?.chatbot?.guidedMode !== false; // default to true

  return (
    <Paper sx={{ p: 3, borderRadius: 2, maxHeight: 'calc(100vh - 160px)', overflow: 'auto' }}>
      <Typography variant="h5" gutterBottom>

      <Typography variant="body2" color="text.secondary" paragraph>

      <Divider sx={{ my: 3 }} />
      
      {/* Basic Assistant Details */}
      <Grid container spacing={3}>
        <Grid item xs={12} md={6}>
          <TextField
            label="Nome do Assistente"
            fullWidth
            value={config?.assistant?.name || ''}
            onChange={(e) => handleAssistantChange('name', e.target.value)}
            margin="normal"

        </Grid>
        <Grid item xs={12} md={6}>
          <TextField
            label="Título do Assistente"
            fullWidth
            value={config?.assistant?.title || ''}
            onChange={(e) => handleAssistantChange('title', e.target.value)}
            margin="normal"
          />
        </Grid>
        <Grid item xs={12}>
          <TextField
            label="Título Completo"
            fullWidth
            value={config?.assistant?.fullTitle || ''}
            onChange={(e) => handleAssistantChange('fullTitle', e.target.value)}
            margin="normal"
            helperText="Título completo usado no prompt do assistente"
          />
        </Grid>
      </Grid>
      
      <Divider sx={{ my: 3 }} />
      
      {/* Guided Mode Section */}
      <Box sx={{ mb: 4 }}>
        <Box sx={{ display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', mb: 2 }}>
          <SmartToyIcon sx={{ fontSize: 28, color: 'primary.main', mr: 1.5 }} />
          <Typography variant="h6" color="primary" sx={{ mb: 0 }}>
            Modo de Conversação
          </Typography>
        </Box>
        
        <FormControlLabel
          control={
            <Switch
              checked={guidedMode}
              onChange={(e) => handleChatbotChange('guidedMode', e.target.checked)}
              color="primary"
            />
          }
          label="Usar modo guiado para agendamentos"
        />
        <FormHelperText>
          {guidedMode ? 
            "O assistente guiará os usuários de forma estruturada no processo de agendamento." :
            "Os usuários poderão conversar livremente com o assistente para agendar horários."}
        </FormHelperText>
        
        {!hasOpenAI && !guidedMode && (
          <Alert severity="warning" sx={{ mt: 2 }}>

          </Alert>

      </Box>
      
      {/* Additional Guided Mode Settings */}
      {guidedMode && (
        <Box sx={{ mb: 4 }}>

          <Grid container spacing={3}>

                    label="Período de Datas Disponíveis"

                    <MenuItem value={7}>7 dias</MenuItem>

                    <MenuItem value={30}>30 dias</MenuItem>
                    <MenuItem value={60}>60 dias</MenuItem>
                  </Select>
                  <FormHelperText>
                    Período de datas futuras que serão exibidas para agendamento

                </FormControl>
              </Box>
            </Grid>
            
            <Grid item xs={12} md={6}>
              <Box sx={{ display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', mb: 1 }}>
                <AccessTimeIcon sx={{ color: 'text.secondary', mr: 1 }} />
                <FormControl fullWidth>
                  <InputLabel id="time-interval-label">Intervalo de Horários</InputLabel>
                  <Select
                    labelId="time-interval-label"
                    value={timeInterval}
                    label="Intervalo de Horários"
                    onChange={(e) => handleChatbotChange('timeInterval', e.target.value)}
                  >
                    <MenuItem value={5}>5 minutos</MenuItem>
                    <MenuItem value={10}>10 minutos</MenuItem>
                    <MenuItem value={15}>15 minutos</MenuItem>
                    <MenuItem value={20}>20 minutos</MenuItem>
                    <MenuItem value={30}>30 minutos</MenuItem>
                    <MenuItem value={60}>60 minutos</MenuItem>
                  </Select>
                  <FormHelperText>
                    Intervalo entre horários disponíveis para agendamento
                  </FormHelperText>
                </FormControl>
              </Box>
            </Grid>
          </Grid>
        </Box>
      )}
      
      {/* Greetings & Prompt */}
      <Grid container spacing={3}>
        <Grid item xs={12}>
          <TextField
            label="Mensagem de Boas-vindas"
            fullWidth
            value={config?.assistant?.greeting || ''}
            onChange={(e) => handleAssistantChange('greeting', e.target.value)}
            margin="normal"
            multiline
            rows={2}
          />
        </Grid>
        
        {/* Only show prompt field if OpenAI is configured */}
        {hasOpenAI && (
          <Grid item xs={12}>
            <TextField
              label="Prompt do Assistente"
              fullWidth
              value={config?.assistant?.prompt || ''}
              onChange={(e) => handleAssistantChange('prompt', e.target.value)}
              margin="normal"
              multiline
              rows={15}
              helperText="Instruções detalhadas para o comportamento do assistente (apenas usado no modo livre)"
            />
          </Grid>
        )}
      </Grid>
    </Paper>
  );

# Chatbot Tests

This directory contains tests for the chatbot component and related utilities.

## Available Tests

The following test files are available:

- `Chatbox.test.js`: Tests for the main Chatbox component
- `ChatbotFixesTest.js`: Specific tests for the fixes implemented in the chatbot
- `../utils/__tests__/bookingUtils.test.js`: Tests for booking utility functions
- `../utils/__tests__/dateUtils.test.js`: Tests for date and time utility functions

## Running Tests

You can run the tests using npm scripts:

```bash
# Run all tests
npm test

# Run only chatbot-related tests
npm run test:chatbot

# Run only chatbot utility tests
npm run test:utils

# Run only the tests for the specific fixes
npm run test:fixes
```

## Key Areas Tested

The tests cover the following key areas:

1. **Date Handling**
   - Correct day of week determination
   - Proper date formatting
   - Date range generation

2. **Business Hours Determination**
   - Different hours for weekdays, Saturdays, and Sundays
   - Fallback to openHours/closeHours when specific weekday hours not defined

3. **Time Slot Generation**
   - Generating time slots based on business hours
   - Using configurable time intervals

4. **Conflict Detection**
   - Detecting overlaps between appointments
   - Handling minimal overlaps (allowing slots with < 5 minute overlap)

5. **UI Formatting**
   - Grouping time slots by hour when there are many
   - Displaying time slots in a user-friendly way

## When to Run These Tests

Run these tests whenever you make changes to:

- The Chatbox component
- Date or time handling logic
- Appointment conflict detection
- Time slot generation
- UI formatting of dates or times

This will ensure that your changes don't break the core chatbot functionality.

## Adding New Tests

When adding new features or making other changes to the chatbot, consider adding new tests to cover:

1. New utility functions
2. Edge cases in date/time handling
3. Changes to the chat flow
4. UI formatting changes

I've implemented a key improvement to the chatbot's experience:

1. When the user selects a date that has no available times, now the chatbot will:
   - Show a message "Não há horários disponíveis para [date]. Gostaria de escolher outra data?"
   - Automatically display the available dates again
   - Reset to the date selection step (step 4) to allow the user to continue the booking flow

2. This improves the UX in several ways:
   - Informs the user clearly about the lack of available times
   - Doesn't abandon the user in a dead-end
   - Automatically suggests the next action (choosing another date)
   - Shows alternate dates immediately without requiring the user to respond

3. The implementation updates:
   - Modified `formatTimeOptionsMessage()` to provide a better experience when no times are available
   - Updated the `handleDateSelect()` function to detect when time slots are empty after filtering
   - Properly redirected the flow back to date selection when no times are available
   - Disabled the old behavior that would attempt to force default times on weekdays

These changes provide a much better user experience when no times are available for a selected date.
